To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the aromatic sidechain ring rotations are dominated by the torsion about the bond to the beta-carbon and that the ring rotations occur in a concerted manner, with the phenyl ring and the phenolic hydroxyl group moving in opposite directions.

the internal dynamics of the tyrosine sidechains in PTB are dominated by torsional oscillations, that these torsional oscillations have a characteristic frequency of 10(11) s(-1), and that the long time dynamics of the aromatic sidechains are dominated by transitions between the two lowest energy conformers.

(i) the high frequency motions of the tyrosines in PTI can be understood as torsional oscillations about a single equilibrium configuration; (ii) the low-frequency ring rotations are best described by a set of discrete states, and the transitions between these states can be characterized by transition state theory; and (iii) the transition-state trajectories provide a detailed description of the ring rotation process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of aromatic sidechain motions in proteins, and the methods used are molecular dynamics simulation and adiabatic transition-state trajectories.
the development and application of methods for the analysis of the internal motions of proteins.
the internal dynamics of protein molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tyrosine rings in PTI are not rigidly fixed in the crystal structure.
the internal dynamics of the tyrosines in PTI are dominated by torsional oscillations, and that the ring rotations are relatively rare.
the tyrosine sidechains of PTI are very mobile, and this mobility may play a role in the function of this protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aromatic sidechain motions in PTI are highly restricted, with the ring orientations being essentially fixed.
the aromatic ring rotations are very slow, and that the motions are strongly coupled with the rest of the molecule.
the tyrosines in PTI undergo rapid oscillations about their equilibrium conformations, while the long-time motions are characterized by a single ring-rotation mode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of proteins are not just a matter of the protein's overall structure, but also of its chemical structure.
the internal dynamics of a protein can be studied by a combination of molecular dynamics and transition-state theory, and that this approach can be used to obtain a detailed picture of the dynamics.
the dynamics of aromatic sidechains are very complex and cannot be described in simple terms.
